177	  // The Meet Rule's closed-trait case, for fa and ga without static parameters, whose
178	  // domains overlap and neither of which is below the other: the declarations hs, each
179	  // below both, together hold every value of the overlap.  The overlap is cut by the
180	  // comprises clauses of the closed traits in it, a trait read as the union of its
181	  // listed types; a part two of whose types exclude is empty; every other part must be
182	  // below the domain of one of hs.  What it cannot show is not covered: a part with no
183	  // closed trait left to cut, a cut that repeats a part on its own path, and a search
184	  // longer than coverageCuts cuts.  A local judgement of overload checking: its result
185	  // is never a subtyping fact.
186	  private val coverageCuts = 1000
187	
188	  def coversOverlap(fa: ArrowType, ga: ArrowType, hs: List[ArrowType]): Boolean = {
189	    def ground(a: ArrowType) = getStaticParams(a).isEmpty
190	    if (hs.isEmpty || !ground(fa) || !ground(ga) || !hs.forall(ground)) return false
191	    def positions(d: Type): Option[List[Type]] = d match {
192	      case STupleType(_, es, None, Nil) => Some(es)
193	      case _: TupleType => None
194	      case t => Some(List(t))
195	    }
196	    type Part = List[List[Type]]
197	    def canon(cs: List[Type]): List[Type] = cs.distinct.sortBy(_.toString)
198	    def conj(cs: List[Type]): Type = makeMaybeIntersectionType(toJavaList(cs))
199	    def asType(p: Part): Type = p match {
200	      case List(cs) => conj(cs)
201	      case _ => makeTupleType(toJavaList(p.map(conj)))
202	    }
203	    def empty(p: Part) = p.exists(cs => cs.exists(a => cs.exists(b => !(a eq b) && ta.definitelyExcludes(a, b))))
204	    val hds = hs.map(sa.makeDomainWithSelfFromArrow)
205	    def covered(p: Part) = { val t = asType(p); hds.exists(h => ta.lteq(t, h)) }
206	    // A closed trait's listed types, its static arguments substituted; a functional
207	    // method's self type is read as its trait.
208	    def listed(t: Type): Option[List[Type]] = t match {
209	      case tt: TraitType => ta.typeCons(tt.getName) match {
210	        case ti: ProperTraitIndex if !ti.comprisesTypes.isEmpty && !NU.isComprisesEllipses(ti.ast) =>
211	          val cs = ta.comprisesClause(tt)
212	          if (cs.size != ti.comprisesTypes.size) None else Some(canon(cs.toList))
213	        case _ => None
214	      }
215	      case ts: TraitSelfType => listed(ts.getNamed)
216	      case _ => None
217	    }
218	    (positions(sa.makeDomainWithSelfFromArrow(fa)), positions(sa.makeDomainWithSelfFromArrow(ga))) match {
219	      case (Some(fs), Some(gs)) if fs.size == gs.size =>
220	        var cuts = 0
221	        var work: List[(Part, Set[Part])] = List((fs.zip(gs).map { case (a, b) => canon(List(a, b)) }, Set[Part]()))
222	        while (!work.isEmpty) {
223	          val (p, path) = work.head
224	          work = work.tail
225	          if (!empty(p) && !covered(p)) {
226	            val cut = p.indices.view.flatMap(i => p(i).view.flatMap(c => listed(c).map(ls => (i, c, ls)))).headOption
227	            cut match {
228	              case None => return false
229	              case Some((i, c, ls)) =>
230	                cuts += 1
231	                if (cuts > coverageCuts || path.contains(p)) return false
232	                work = ls.map(l => (p.updated(i, canon(p(i).filter(_ != c) :+ l)), path + p)) ++ work
233	            }
234	          }
235	        }
236	        true
237	      case _ => false
238	    }
239	  }

359	  sealed trait COMPARISON_RESULT {}
360	  case object NO_RELATION extends COMPARISON_RESULT {}
361	  case object OVERLOADS extends COMPARISON_RESULT {}
362	  case object NARROWS extends COMPARISON_RESULT {}
363	  case object JUST_SHADOWS extends COMPARISON_RESULT {}
364	  
365	  def compare(f: Functional, g: Functional): COMPARISON_RESULT = (f, g) match {
366	    case (f: HasSelfType, g: HasSelfType) =>
367	      val (fPTSS, tFST, fSI) = paramTypeWithoutSelf(f)
368	      val fST = removeSelf(tFST)
369	      val (uGPTSS, uGST, gSI) = paramTypeWithoutSelf(g)
370	      if(fSI != gSI)
371	        return NO_RELATION
372	      val (fSPJ, gSPJ) = (f.staticParameters, g.staticParameters)
373	      val (fSPS, gSPS) = (toList(fSPJ), toList(gSPJ))
374	      val (fSA, gSA) = (staticParamsToArgs(fSPJ), staticParamsToArgs(gSPJ))
375	      val (fTA, gTA) = (ta.extend(gSPS, None), ta.extend(fSPS, None))
376	      if(!staticArgsMatchStaticParams(toList(fSA), gSPS)(fTA) || 
377	         !staticArgsMatchStaticParams(toList(gSA), fSPS)(gTA))
378	        return NO_RELATION
379	      val fSA_for_gSP = new StaticTypeReplacer(fSPJ, gSA)
380	      val (gPTSS, gST) = (fSA_for_gSP.replaceIn(uGPTSS), fSA_for_gSP.replaceIn(removeSelf(uGST)))
381	      val (fRT, gRT) = (f.getReturnType.unwrap, fSA_for_gSP.replaceIn(g.getReturnType.unwrap))
382	      val fST_strictlySub_gST = isTrue(fTA.subtype(fST, gST)) && !isTrue(fTA.subtype(gST,fST))
383	      val gDTSS_sub_fDTSS = isTrue(fTA.subtype(gPTSS, fPTSS))
384	      val fDTSS_sub_gDTSS = isTrue(fTA.subtype(fPTSS, gPTSS))
385	      val fRT_eq_gRT = isTrue(fTA.equivalent(fRT, gRT))
386	      (fST_strictlySub_gST, gDTSS_sub_fDTSS, fDTSS_sub_gDTSS, fRT_eq_gRT) match {
387	        case (false, _, _, _) => NO_RELATION
388	        case (true, true, false, _) => JUST_SHADOWS
389	        case (true, true, true, false) => NARROWS
390	        case (true, true, true, true) => OVERLOADS
391	      }
392	    case _ =>
393	      bug("Should only be used on methods and functional methods.")
394	  }
395	  
396	  def narrows(f: Functional, g: Functional) = compare(f, g) match {
397	    case NARROWS => true
398	    case _ => false
399	  }
400	  
401	  def shadows(f: Functional, g: Functional) = compare(f, g) match {
402	    case NO_RELATION => false
403	    case _ => true
404	  }
405	  
406	  def overloads(f: Functional, g: Functional) = compare(f, g) match {
407	    case OVERLOADS => true
408	    case _ => false
409	  }

412	    case STraitSelfType(_, tt, _) => tt
413	    case _ => x

42	 * subtyping, alpha renaming, checking for equality up to renaming and 
43	 * so forth.
44	 * 
45	 * The biggest weakness of this implementation is that we do
46	 * not syntactically distinguish types and type schema.

127	       * from t. Then strip t of it's type parameters to get t'

132	    // s has static parameters and t does not

134	      /* Try and infer an instantiation sigma of s such that 
135	       * sigma(s) <: t */
136	      val nta = ta.extend(getStaticParams(s), getWhere(s))

177	  def subEDsolution(s: Type, t: Type): Option[(Type, List[StaticArg])]  =  {
178	//    println("subED:\n   " + s + "[" + getStaticParams(s) + "]\n   " + t + "[" + getStaticParams(t) + "]")
179	    val result = (s,t) match {

182	      /* Extend the type analyzer with the static parameters
183	       * from s. Then strip s of it's type parameters to get s'
184	       * and call lteq(s',t) */
185	      val tsa = extend(getStaticParams(s), getWhere(s))
186	      val ss = clearStaticParams(s)
187	      tsa.subEDsolution(ss, t)
188	    // s has static parameters and t does not
189	    case (s, t) if !t.getInfo.getStaticParams.isEmpty =>
190	      /* Try and infer an instantiation sigma of t such that 
191	       * s <: sigma(t) */
192	      val nta = ta.extend(getStaticParams(t), getWhere(t))
193	      def constraintMaker(tt: Type, m: Map[Op, Op]) = nta.subtype(s, tt)
194	      val helperResult = inferStaticParamsHelper(t, constraintMaker, true, true)

196	      helperResult

198	    case (s,t) => if (ta.lteq(s, t)) Some((t, List[StaticArg]())) else None

269	  /**
270	   * Checks if two types `s` and `t` are syntactically equivalent. If either
271	   * type has static parameters, then the `syntacticEqGeneric` method is called.
272	   * Otherwise, a simply equality check is performed on the types.
273	   */
274	  def syntacticEq(s: Type, t: Type): Boolean =
275	    if (!s.getInfo.getStaticParams.isEmpty() || !t.getInfo.getStaticParams.isEmpty())
276	      syntacticEqGeneric(s, t)
277	    else
278	      s == t

280	  /**
281	   * Checks if two type schema `s` and `t` are syntactically equivalent under
282	   * alpha renaming. The static params of `s` are used to instantiate `t` and
283	   * `t`'s bounds; if the instantiated type and bounds are syntactically
284	   * equivalent to those of `s`, then the two type schema `s` and `t` are
285	   * syntactically equivalent.
286	   */
287	  protected def syntacticEqGeneric(s: Type, t: Type): Boolean = {
288	    
289	    // Extract out the explicit static params of each.
290	    // TODO: What to do about lifted static params?
291	    val s_sp = getStaticParams(s).filterNot(_.isLifted)
292	    val t_sp = getStaticParams(t).filterNot(_.isLifted)
293	    
294	    // If they don't match in kind, return false.
295	    if (!equalKinds(s_sp, t_sp)) return false
296	    
297	    // Get the list of bounds on the static params. Each elt is Some(b) iff that
298	    // static param is a type parameter.
299	    val s_bds = s_sp.map(staticParamBoundType)
300	    val t_bds = t_sp.map(staticParamBoundType)
301	    
302	    // Create the StaticParam -> StaticArg replacement list. t's static params
303	    // will map to s's static params' corresponding static args.
304	    val s_sp_args = s_sp.map(staticParamToArg)
305

442	  protected def boundsSubstitution(phi: Type => Type,
443	                                   sparams: List[StaticParam])
444	                                   : Option[List[StaticParam]] = {
445	    import scala.collection.mutable.HashMap
446	    
447	    // Create a mapping from type variables in the static params to IMAGES OF their
448	    // corresponding bounds.
449	    val varsMap = new HashMap[VarType, List[Type]]
450	    for (SStaticParam(info, _, x:Id, exts, _, _, _, _:KindType, _) <- sparams)      // TODO: variance needs to be addressed
451	      varsMap(NF.makeVarType(info.getSpan, x)) = exts.map(phi)
452	    
453	//    println("boundsSubstitution on " + sparams)
454	    // Get the unique vars in the image under phi.
455	    val imageVars = varsMap.keys.map(phi).filter(_.isInstanceOf[VarType])
456	                           .toList.distinct.map(_.asInstanceOf[VarType])
457	//    println("  imageVars = " + imageVars)
458	    
459	    // Transfer bounds from the image vars onto the preimage vars to produce
460	    // a new set of static params.
461	    val imageSparams = imageVars map { y =>
462	      
463	      // For each x that maps to y under phi, collect the image of its bound.
464	      val ybds = (for ((x, xbds) <- varsMap ; if phi(x) == y) yield xbds)
465	                   .toList.flatten.map(_.asInstanceOf[BaseType])
466	      
467	      // Create the static param for Y <: YBDS.
468	      NF.makeTypeParam(NU.getSpan(y), y.getName, toJavaList(ybds), none[Type], false)
469	    }
470	//    println("  imageSparams = " + imageSparams)
471	    
472	    // The bounds are kept as the list they are, each already a BaseType, without
473	    // Any and duplicates, and never met into one type: the meet of bounds one of
474	    // which is a trait with a comprises clause can be a union, which a bound
475	    // list cannot hold, and normalizing it expands that trait into its members.
476	    val rimageSparams = imageSparams.map{
477	      case SStaticParam(i, v, x, e, doms, d, a, k:KindType, l) =>
478	        val bds = removeDuplicates(e.filterNot(_.isInstanceOf[AnyType])).map(_.asInstanceOf[BaseType])
479	        SStaticParam(i, v, x, bds, doms, d, a, k, l)
480	      case x => x
481	    }
482	//    println("  rimageSparams = " + rimageSparams)
483	    val rimageTa = ta.extend(rimageSparams, None)
484	    // Verify that the image environment can prove that each variable's image
485	    // is a subtype of all its bounds' images, one bound at a time. An image
486	    // variable is a subtype of each bound it was given above without a proof.
487	    // Sizes have no bounds; a nat or int parameter is kept as it is.
488	    val sizeSparams = sparams.filter(sp => sp.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindNat] || sp.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindInt])
489	    def declared(y: Type, b: Type) = rimageSparams.exists {
490	      case SStaticParam(_, _, n, bds, _, _, _, _:KindType, _) =>
491	        y.isInstanceOf[VarType] && y.asInstanceOf[VarType].getName == n && bds.contains(b)
492	      case _ => false
493	    }
494	    if (varsMap.forall { case (x, xbds) =>
495	      xbds.forall(b => b.isInstanceOf[AnyType] || declared(phi(x), phi(b)) || rimageTa.lteq(phi(x), phi(b)))
496	    }) Some(rimageSparams ++ sizeSparams) // Success -- return the image's static params.
497	    else None             // Failure
498	  }

342	      case (None, _) => True
343	      case (Some(s), Some(t)) => sub(s, t)
344	      case _ => False

415	  // dExc's answers in this analyzer, by the question with its inference variables renamed apart:
416	  // an answer is the same under every renaming of them, so a question asked again with fresh
417	  // variables, as each inference makes them, is computed once. An answer is kept only from an empty
418	  // cycle history, marked if its computation read the context, so that a hit on it is a read of the
419	  // context too, and shared through the trait table if it read none; a computation that opened a
420	  // size is not kept.
421	  private final val cacheExclusions = ProjectProperties.getBoolean("fortress.analyzer.exclusion.cache", true)
422	  private val exclusionMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[(Type, Type), (Boolean, Boolean)]()
423	
424	  def dExc(x: Type, y: Type)(implicit history: Set[hType]): Boolean =
425	    if (!cacheExclusions || !history.isEmpty) isTrue(exc(x,y))
426	    else TypeAnalyzer.renamedApart(x, y) match {
427	      case None => isTrue(exc(x,y))
428	      case Some(question) => exclusionMemo.get(question) match {
429	        case Some((v, contextual)) => if (contextual) traits.readContext(); v
430	        case None => traits.sharedExclusion(question) match {
431	          case null =>
432	            val before = traits.contextReads
433	            val opened = openedSizeCount
434	            val result = isTrue(exc(x,y))
435	            if (openedSizeCount == opened) {
436	              val contextual = traits.contextReads != before
437	              exclusionMemo += (question -> (result, contextual))
438	              if (!contextual) traits.shareExclusion(question, result)
439	            }
440	            result
441	          case shared =>
442	            exclusionMemo += (question -> (shared.booleanValue, false))
443	            shared.booleanValue
444	        }
445	      }
446	    }

467	  private val pExcMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[(Type, Type, Boolean, Set[hType]), CFormula]()

469	  protected def pExc(x: Type, y: Type)(implicit negate: Boolean, history: Set[hType]): CFormula = {
470	    if (x == y) pFalse()
471	    else if (cacheExcludes)
472	      traits.groundAnswer(false, x, y, negate) match {
473	        case null => pExcMemo.get((x, y, negate, history)) match {
474	          case Some(v) => traits.readContext(); v
475	          case _ =>
476	            val before = traits.contextReads
477	            val result = pExcInner(x,y)
478	            pExcMemo += ((x, y, negate, history) -> result)
479	            traits.ground(false, x, y, negate, before, result)
480	            result
481	        }
482	        case v => v
483	      }
484	    else pExcInner(x,y)
485	  }

487	  protected def pExcInner(x: Type, y: Type)(implicit negate: Boolean, history: Set[hType]): CFormula = (removeSelf(x), removeSelf(y)) match {
488	    case (s: BottomType, _) => pTrue()
489	    case (_, t: BottomType) => pTrue()
490	    case (s: AnyType, t) => pSub(t, BOTTOM)
491	    case (s, t: AnyType) => pSub(s, BOTTOM)
492	    case (s@SIntersectionType(_, elts), t) =>
493	      pOr(pSub(s, BOTTOM), pOr(elts.map(pExc(_, t))))
494	    case (s, t: IntersectionType) => exc(t, s)
495	    case (s@SUnionType(_, elts), t) =>
496	      pAnd(elts.map(pExc(_, t)))
497	    case (s, t: UnionType) => exc(t, s)
498	    case (i: _InferenceVarType, j: _InferenceVarType) if i==j => pFalse()
499	    case (i: _InferenceVarType, j: _InferenceVarType) => pAnd(pExclusion(i,j), pExclusion(j,i))
500	    case (i: _InferenceVarType, t) => pExclusion(i, t)
501	    case (s, j: _InferenceVarType) => pExc(j, s)
502	    case (s@SVarType(_, sid, _), t@SVarType(_, tid, _)) if (s==t || sid == tid) =>
503	      pOr(pSub(s, BOTTOM), pSub(t, BOTTOM))
504	    case (s@SVarType(_, id, _), t) =>
505	      val hEntry = (negate, false, s, t)
506	      traits.readContext()
507	      if (history.contains(hEntry))
508	        False
509	      else {
510	        val nHistory = history + hEntry
511	        val sParam = staticParam(id)
512	        val supers = pNorm(makeIntersectionType(toListFromImmutable(sParam.getExtendsClause)))
513	        if (negate) pFalse()(!negate) else pExc(supers, t)(negate, nHistory)
514	      }
515	    case (s, t:VarType) => exc(t, s)
516	    // TODO: Check what happens when stem s = stem t
517	    case (s: TraitType, t: TraitType) =>
518	      def checkEC(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = {
519	        def cEC(s: TraitType, t: TraitType) = pOr(excludesClause(s).map(e => withClauseParams(e).pSub(t, e)))
520	        pOr(cEC(s, t), cEC(t, s))
521	      }
522	      def checkCC(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = {
523	        def cCC(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = {
524	          val scc = comprisesClause(s)
525	          pAnd(pFromBoolean(!scc.isEmpty), pAnd(scc.map(pExc(t,_))))
526	        }
527	        pOr(cCC(s, t), cCC(t, s))
528	      }
529	      def checkO(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = {
530	        def cO(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = typeCons(s.getName) match {
531	          case _:ObjectTraitIndex => pSub(s, t)(!negate, history)
532	          case _ => pFalse()
533	        }
534	        pOr(cO(s,t), cO(t,s))
535	      }
536	      def checkP(s: TraitType, t: TraitType): CFormula = {
537	        val sas = ancestors(s) ++ Set(s)
538	        val tas = ancestors(t) ++ Set(t)
539	        def cP(s: BaseType, t: BaseType): CFormula = (s, t) match {
540	          case (s@STraitType(_, n1, a1, _), t@STraitType(_, n2, a2, _)) if (n1 == n2) =>
541	            //Todo: Handle bool args
542	            pOr((a1, a2).zipped.map{
543	              case (STypeArg(_, _, t1), STypeArg(_, _, t2)) => pEqv(t1, t2)(!negate, history)
544	              case (SIntArg(_, _, i1: IntBase), SIntArg(_, _, i2: IntBase)) => pEqv(i1, i2)(!negate)
545	              case _ => pFalse()
546	            })
547	          case _ => pFalse()
548	        }
549	        pOr(for(sa <- sas; ta <- tas) yield cP(sa, ta))
550	      }
551	      pOr(List(checkEC(s,t), checkCC(s,t), checkO(s,t), checkP(s,t)))
552	    // ToDo: Handle keywords. Note that this will mean you can have a tuple of length 1 without varargs.
553	    case (s@STupleType(_, e1, Some(v1), _), t@STupleType(_, e2, mv2, _)) =>
554	        pExc(disjunctFromTuple(s, max(e1.size, e2.size)), t)
555	    case (s@STupleType(_, e1, None, _), t@STupleType(_, e2, Some(v2), _)) => pExc(t, s)
556	    case (STupleType(_, e1, None, _), STupleType(_, e2, None, _)) if (e1.size == e2.size) =>
557	      pOr((e1, e2).zipped.map((a, b) => pExc(a, b)))
558	    case (STupleType(_, e1, None, _), STupleType(_, e2, None, _)) =>
559	      pTrue()
560	    case (s: TupleType, t) => pExc(disjunctFromTuple(s, 1), t)
561	    case (s, t: TupleType) => pExc(t, s)
562	    case (s: ArrowType, t: ArrowType) => pFalse()
563	    case (s: ArrowType, t) => pTrue()
564	    case (s, t: ArrowType) => pExc(t, s)
565	  }

568	    object remover extends Walker {
569	      override def walk(y: Any): Any = y match {
570	        case t:TraitSelfType =>
571	          if (t.getComprised.isEmpty)
572	            t.getNamed
573	          else
574	            NF.makeIntersectionType(t.getNamed, NF.makeMaybeUnionType(t.getComprised))

598	  // Formula.reduce's answers in this analyzer, each marked if its computation read the context.
599	  // A reduction asks only this analyzer's public questions, each from an empty cycle history, so
600	  // its answer depends on the formula and this analyzer alone, and a hit on a marked answer is a
601	  // read of the context too. A reduction that opened a size is not kept: computed again, it
602	  // would open a fresh one.
603	  private final val cacheReduce = ProjectProperties.getBoolean("fortress.analyzer.reduce.cache", true)
604	  private val reduceMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[CFormula, (CFormula, Boolean)]()
605	
606	  def reduced(c: CFormula)(compute: => CFormula): CFormula =
607	    if (!cacheReduce) compute
608	    else reduceMemo.get(c) match {
609	      case Some((v, contextual)) => if (contextual) traits.readContext(); v
610	      case None =>
611	        val before = traits.contextReads
612	        val opened = openedSizeCount
613	        val result = compute
614	        if (openedSizeCount == opened) reduceMemo += (c -> (result, traits.contextReads != before))
615	        result
616	    }

618	  private val normalizeVarTypeMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[Id, Any]()
619	  private val normalizeTraitTypeMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[(Id, List[StaticArg]), Any]()
620	  private val normalizeTupleTypeMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[(List[Type], Option[Type]), Any]()
621	  private val normalizeArrowTypeMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[(Type, Type, Effect, Boolean), Any]()
622	  private val normalizeOtherTypeMemo = new scala.collection.mutable.HashMap[Any, Any]()
623	  // The normalize memos' keys whose value was computed by reading the context: a hit on one
624	  // is a read of the context too.
625	  private val contextualNorms = new scala.collection.mutable.HashSet[Any]()
626	  private def noteNorm(k: Any): Unit = if (contextualNorms.contains(k)) traits.readContext()
627	  private def markNorm(before: Long, ks: Any*): Unit = if (traits.contextReads != before) contextualNorms ++= ks

629	  def normalize(x: Type): Type = pNorm(x)(Set[hType]())

631	  protected def pNorm(x: Type)(implicit history: Set[hType]): Type = {
632	    object normalizer extends Walker {
633	      override def walk(y: Any): Any = y match {
634	        case t: VarType => walkVarType(t)
635	        case t: TraitType => walkTraitType(t)
636	        case t: TupleType => walkTupleType(t)
637	        case t: ArrowType => walkArrowType(t)
638	        case _ => walkOtherType(y)
639	      }
640	      def walkVarType(t: VarType) = {
641	        t match { case SVarType(_, n, _) =>
642	            if (cacheNormalizeVar)
643	              normalizeVarTypeMemo.get(n) match {
644	                case Some(v) => noteNorm(n); v
645	                case _ =>
646	                  val before = traits.contextReads
647	                  val result = walkVarTypeInner(t, n)
648	                  normalizeVarTypeMemo += (n -> result)
649	                  markNorm(before, n)
650	                  result
651	              }
652	            else walkVarTypeInner(t, n)
653	        }
654	      }
655	      def walkVarTypeInner(t: VarType, n: Id) = super.walk(t)
656	      def walkTraitType(t: TraitType) = {
657	        t match { case STraitType(_, n, a, _) =>
658	            if (cacheNormalizeTrait) {
659	              normalizeTraitTypeMemo.get((n, a)) match {
660	                case Some(v) => noteNorm((n, a)); v
661	                case _ =>
662	                  val before = traits.contextReads
663	                  walkTraitTypeInner(t, n, a) match {
664	                    case result@STraitType(_, _, aa, _) =>
665	                       normalizeTraitTypeMemo += ((n, a) -> result)
666	                       normalizeTraitTypeMemo += ((n, aa) -> result)
667	                       markNorm(before, (n, a), (n, aa))
668	                       result
669	                  }
670	              }
671	            }
672	            else walkTraitTypeInner(t, n, a)
673	        }
674	      }
675	      def walkTraitTypeInner(t: TraitType, n: Id, a: List[StaticArg]) = {
676	        typeCons(n) match {
677	          case ti: TypeAliasIndex =>
678	            val params = toListFromImmutable(ti.staticParameters)
679	            walk(substitute(a, params, ti.ast.getTypeDef))
680	          case _ => super.walk(t)
681	        }
682	      }
683	      def walkTupleType(t: TupleType) = {
684	        if (cacheNormalizeTuple)
685	          t match { case STupleType(_, e, vt, _) =>
686	              normalizeTupleTypeMemo.get((e, vt)) match {
687	                case Some(v) => noteNorm((e, vt)); v
688	                case _ =>
689	                  val before = traits.contextReads
690	                  walkTupleTypeInner(t) match {
691	                    case result@STupleType(_, ee, vtx, _) =>
692	                      normalizeTupleTypeMemo += ((e, vt) -> result)
693	                      normalizeTupleTypeMemo += ((ee, vtx) -> result)
694	                      markNorm(before, (e, vt), (ee, vtx))
695	                      result
696	                    case result =>
697	                      normalizeTupleTypeMemo += ((e, vt) -> result)
698	                      markNorm(before, (e, vt))
699	                      result
700	                  }
701	              }
702	          }
703	        else walkTupleTypeInner(t)
704	      }
705	      def walkTupleTypeInner(t: TupleType) = {
706	        //ToDo: Handle keywords
707	        super.walk(t) match {
708	          case STupleType(i, e, Some(v: BottomType), k) => STupleType(i, e, None, k)
709	          case STupleType(i, e, vt, k) if e.contains(bottom) => bottom
710	          case STupleType(i, e, None, Nil) if (e.size == 1) => e.head
711	          case _ => t
712	        }
713	      }
714	      def walkArrowType(t: ArrowType) = {
715	        if (cacheNormalizeArrow)
716	          t match { case SArrowType(_, d, r, e, i, _) =>
717	              normalizeArrowTypeMemo.get((d, r, e, i)) match {
718	                case Some(v) => noteNorm((d, r, e, i)); v
719	                case _ =>
720	                  val before = traits.contextReads
721	                  walkArrowTypeInner(t) match {
722	                    case result@SArrowType(_, dd, rr, ee, ii, _) =>
723	                      normalizeArrowTypeMemo += ((d, r, e, i) -> result)
724	                      normalizeArrowTypeMemo += ((dd, rr, ee, ii) -> result)
725	                      markNorm(before, (d, r, e, i), (dd, rr, ee, ii))
726	                      result
727	                  }
728	              }
729	          }
730	        else walkArrowTypeInner(t)
731	      }
732	      def walkArrowTypeInner(t: ArrowType) = super.walk(t)
733	      def walkOtherType(t: Any) = {
734	        if (cacheNormalizeOther)
735	          normalizeOtherTypeMemo.get(t) match {
736	            case Some(v) => noteNorm(t); v
737	            case _ =>
738	              val before = traits.contextReads
739	              val result = walkOtherTypeInner(t)
740	              normalizeOtherTypeMemo += (t -> result)
741	              markNorm(before, t)
742	              result
743	          }
744	        else walkOtherTypeInner(t)
745	      }
746	      def walkOtherTypeInner(t: Any) = t match {
747	        case u@SUnionType(_, e) =>
748	          val ps = e.flatMap(t => disjuncts(walk(t).asInstanceOf[Type]))
749	          makeUnionType(normDisjunct(ps))
750	        case i@SIntersectionType(_, e) =>
751	          val sop = cross(e.map(t => disjuncts(walk(t).asInstanceOf[Type])))
752	          val ps = sop.map(t => makeIntersectionType(normConjunct(t.flatMap(disjuncts))))
753	          makeUnionType(normDisjunct(ps))
754	        case o:Op => normalize(o)
755	        case _ => super.walk(t)
756	      }
757	    }
758	    // Here's the body: walk the type, and make sure it's a type when finished
759	    normalizer(x).asInstanceOf[Type]
760	  }

762	  protected def normConjunct(x: Iterable[Type])(implicit history: Set[hType]): List[Type] = {
763	    // A closed trait is replaced by the types its comprises clause lists that no other
764	    // conjunct excludes, only where that conjunct names no type or inference variable:
765	    // over a variable the union would be split by the union rule before the variable's
766	    // bound is read, and a solution that holds only of the union as a whole is lost.
767	    def excludedListed(c: Type) =
768	      x.exists(z => getVarTypes(z).isEmpty && !hasInferenceVars(z) && dExc(z, c))
769	    val cc = x.map(y => (y, y.isInstanceOf[TraitType] &&
770	                            comprisesClause(y.asInstanceOf[TraitType]).exists(excludedListed))).toList
771	    if (cc.exists(_._2))
772	      cc.map(z => { val (y, p) = z;
773	                    if (p) makeUnionType(comprisesClause(y.asInstanceOf[TraitType]).toList.flatMap(c => if (excludedListed(c)) None else Some(c)))
774	                    else y })
775	    else if (x.exists(y => x.exists(z => dExc(y, z))))
776	      List(BOTTOM)
777	    else {
778	      val ds = x.foldLeft(List[Type]())((l, a) => {
779	        val l2 = l.filter(x => !isTrue(sub(a, x)))
780	        l2 ++ (if (l2.exists(x => isTrue(sub(x, a)))) Nil else List(a))
781	      })
782	      val es = ds.map(_ match {
783	        case t:TupleType => Left(t)
784	        case s => Right(s)
785	      })
786	      val (ts, ss) = (for (Left(x) <- es) yield x, for (Right(x) <- es) yield x)
787	      ss ++ normTuples(ts)
788	    }
789	  }

791	  protected def normTuples(ts: List[TupleType])(implicit history: Set[hType]): List[TupleType] = ts match {
792	    case Nil => Nil
793	    case _ => List(ts.reduceLeft((a,b) => normTuples(a,b)))
794	  }

797	  protected def normTuples(x: TupleType, y: TupleType)(implicit history: Set[hType]): TupleType = (x,y) match {
798	    case (STupleType(_, e1, None, _), STupleType(_, e2, None, _)) =>
799	      STupleType(makeInfo(e1), (e1, e2).zipped.map((a,b) => pMeet(a,b)), None, Nil)
800	    case (STupleType(_, e1, None, _), STupleType(_, e2, Some(_), _)) =>
801	      normTuples(x, disjunctFromTuple(y, e1.size).asInstanceOf[TupleType])
802	    case (STupleType(_, e1, Some(_), _), STupleType(_, e2, None, _)) =>
803	      normTuples(disjunctFromTuple(x, e2.size).asInstanceOf[TupleType], y)
804	    case (STupleType(_, e1, Some(v1), _), STupleType(_, e2, Some(v2), _)) => {
805	      val ee1 = e1 ++ List.fill(e2.size - e1.size){v1}
806	      val ee2 = e2 ++ List.fill(e1.size - e2.size){v2}
807	      STupleType(makeInfo(e1), (ee1, ee2).zipped.map((a,b) => pMeet(a,b)), Some(pMeet(v1, v2)), Nil)
808	    }
809	  }

811	  protected def normDisjunct(xx: Iterable[Type])(implicit history: Set[hType]): List[Type] = {
812	      val x = xx.toList

==> explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <==
#!/bin/bash
# The distance stage's comparison: this table (run.sh's) against the last landed one.
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh <last-landed-table|""> <this-table>
#
# Prints one verdict line, then every #kind and #class row whose count moved, with the
# change, and every #crash row that went or came. It is REPORTED and never red: it always
# exits 0, whatever moved, a stale shadow and a run that produced no table included (Pavol,
# answer 11, POSITIONS.md 2026-09-26: a report-only stage, whose job is driving the distance
# down). The verdicts:
#   DISTANCE DOWN|UP|SAME   <last> -> <now>
#   DISTANCE FIRST          no landed table to compare with
#   DISTANCE NO TABLE       this run produced no count, with the table's own reason
#   SETTING CHANGED         the two tables ran different settings: the counts are not like for like
#   SHADOW STALE            a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources
# A move of 2 to 4 errors in the components' type errors or in which pair of LEXICO, SQCAP or
# INVERSE declarations an overloading error names is the checker's run-to-run variation
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md section 5), not a change; a crash row whose line numbers
# moved because a rung edited above it prints as one gone and one new.
set -u
OLD=${1:-}; NEW=${2:?usage: compare.sh <last-landed-table> <this-table>}
field () { awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '$1 == t { sub("^[^\t]*\t", ""); print; exit }' "$2" ; }

now=$(field '#total' "$NEW")
sh=$(field '#shadow' "$NEW")
case "$sh" in STALE*) echo "SHADOW STALE   ${sh#STALE: }" ;; esac
case "$now" in
  ''|none*) echo "DISTANCE NO TABLE   ${now:-no #total row}" ; exit 0 ;;
esac
if [ -z "$OLD" ] || [ ! -f "$OLD" ] ; then
    echo "DISTANCE FIRST   $now distinct errors, $(field '#distance' "$NEW" | cut -d';' -f1); no landed table to compare with"
    exit 0
fi
was=$(field '#total' "$OLD")
ws=$(field '#distance' "$OLD" | cut -d';' -f1); ns=$(field '#distance' "$NEW" | cut -d';' -f1)
[ "$ws" = "$ns" ] || echo "SETTING CHANGED   was $ws, now $ns: the counts below are not like for like"
case "$was" in ''|none*) echo "DISTANCE $now, the landed table has no count (${was:-no #total row})" ; exit 0 ;; esac
if   [ "$now" -lt "$was" ] ; then echo "DISTANCE DOWN   $was -> $now ($((now - was)))"
elif [ "$now" -gt "$was" ] ; then echo "DISTANCE UP   $was -> $now (+$((now - was)))"
else echo "DISTANCE SAME   $now" ; fi

component GenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk
export Executable

(* Two generic declarations over P[T] and Box[T] and over Q[T] and Box[T], where P[T] excludes Q[T] at one T and the object Box fixes one T for both, exclude each other, so they are a valid overloading and each call runs the one its arguments select (overloading.tex, section "Declarations with Static Parameters"). *)

trait P[\T\] excludes { Q[\T\] } end
trait Q[\T\] end
object Mixed extends { P[\ZZ32\], Q[\String\] } end
object Box[\T\] end

o[\T\](x: P[\T\], b: Box[\T\]): String = "oP"
o[\T\](x: Q[\T\], b: Box[\T\]): String = "oQ"

trait PN[\nat n\] excludes { QN[\n\] } end
trait QN[\nat n\] end
object MixedN extends { PN[\3\], QN[\4\] } end
object BoxN[\nat n\] end

r[\T\](x: P[\T\], b: Box[\T\]): String = "rP"
r[\U\](x: Q[\U\], b: Box[\U\]): String = "rQ"

s[\nat n\](x: PN[\n\], b: BoxN[\n\]): String = "sP"
s[\nat m\](x: QN[\m\], b: BoxN[\m\]): String = "sQ"

run(): () = do
    assert(o(Mixed, Box[\ZZ32\]), "oP", "a Mixed is a P of ZZ32 and a Q of String, so with a Box of ZZ32 only the declaration over P applies")
    assert(o(Mixed, Box[\String\]), "oQ", "with a Box of String only the declaration over Q applies")
    assert(r(Mixed, Box[\ZZ32\]), "rP", "renamed static parameters: with a Box of ZZ32 only the declaration over P applies")
    assert(r(Mixed, Box[\String\]), "rQ", "renamed static parameters: with a Box of String only the declaration over Q applies")
    assert(s(MixedN, BoxN[\3\]), "sP", "size parameters: with a BoxN of 3 only the declaration over PN applies")
    assert(s(MixedN, BoxN[\4\]), "sQ", "size parameters: with a BoxN of 4 only the declaration over QN applies")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

trait SequentialGenerator[\E\] extends { Generator[\E\] }
        excludes { HasRank }
    getter asString(): String = "seq(" (self asif Generator[\E\]).asString ")"
    seq(self): SequentialGenerator[\E\] = self
    map[\G\](f: E->G): SequentialGenerator[\G\] =
        SimpleMappedSeqGenerator[\E,G\](self,f)
    (* TODO: make overloaded *)
    nest[\G\](f: E -> Generator[\G\]): Generator[\G\] =
        typecase f of
            f':E -> SequentialGenerator[\G\] =>
                SimpleNestedSeqGenerator[\E,G\](self,f')
            else => SimpleNestedGenerator[\E,G\](self,f)
        end
    (* TODO: make overloaded *)
    cross[\F\](g:Generator[\F\]): Generator[\(E,F)\] =
        typecase g of
            g':SequentialGenerator[\F\] =>
                    SimplePairSeqGenerator[\E,F\](self,g')
            else => SimplePairGenerator[\E,F\](self,g)
        end
    negate(): Matrix[\T,s0,s1\] = (-mem).t()

\seclabel{overloading-terms}

Fortress allows multiple functional declarations of the same name to
be declared in a single scope.  However, recall from \chapref{names}
the following shadowing rules:
\begin{itemize}
\item
dotted method declarations shadow top-level function declarations with
the same name, and
\item
dotted method declarations provided by a trait or object declaration
or object expression
shadow functional method declarations with the same name that are
provided by a different trait or object declaration
or object expression.
\end{itemize}
Also, note that a trait or object declaration
or object expression must not have a
functional method declaration and a dotted method declaration with the
same name, either directly or by inheritance.
Therefore, top-level functions can overload
with other top-level functions and functional methods,
dotted methods with other dotted methods,
and functional methods with other functional methods and top-level functions.
It is a static error if any top-level function declaration is
more specific than any functional method declaration.
If a top-level function declaration is overloaded with a functional method
declaration, the top-level function declaration must not be more specific than
the functional method declaration.


Operator declarations with the same name but different fixity
are not a valid overloading; they are unambiguous declarations.
An operator method declaration whose name is one of the operator parameters
(described in \secref{opr-ident})
of its enclosing trait or object may be overloaded with other operator
declarations in the same component.
Therefore, such an operator method declaration
must satisfy the overloading rules
(described in \chapref{overloaded-declarations})
with every operator declaration in the same component.

\note{This restriction will be relaxed.}

Declarations with the same functional name may have different static
parameters, or some of them may have static parameters and others none.
A declaration with static parameters is read as one declaration whose
parameter type ranges over every instance of it whose static arguments
satisfy their bounds: it is applicable to a call when some such instance is
(\secref{functional-applicability}), and it is compared with other
declarations on the parameter types they declare, taken over all their
instances (\secref{resolving-overloading}).
A declaration without static parameters is the case with none.
The rules that a set of such declarations must satisfy are given in
\chapref{overloaded-declarations}.
\revision{revival-overloading}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said here that
declarations of one name may not differ in their static parameters, nor may one
have static parameters and another not, so that static parameters do not enter
into applicability.
Neither implementation enforced that: the interpreter has overloaded
declarations with different static parameters since 2007, and the compiled type
checker applies to them the rules of the type group's paper of 2011, which reads
the parameter type of a declaration with static parameters as quantified over
them; \library\ overload across different static parameters throughout.
This chapter and \chapref{overloaded-declarations} now state that model.}

We also use \emph{function declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$} to refer to a
function declaration with function name $\f$, parameter type $\Ps$,
and return type $\Us$.


For method declarations, we must take into account the self parameter,
as follows:

A \emph{dotted method declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps):\Us$} is a dotted
method declaration with name $f$, where $\Ps_0$ is the trait or object
type in which the declaration appears, $\Ps$ is the parameter type,
and $\Us$ is the return type.  (Note that despite the suggestive
notation, a dotted method declaration does not explicitly list its
self parameter.)

A \emph{functional method declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$ with self
parameter at $i$} is a functional method declaration with name $f$,
with the parameter \EXP{\mathord{\KWD{self}}} in the $i$th position
of the parameter type $\Ps$, and return type $\Us$.  Note that the static
type of the self parameter is the trait or object trait type in which
the declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$ occurs.  In the following, we will use
$\Ps_i$ to refer to the $i$th element of $\Ps$.

We elide the return type of a declaration, writing $\f(\Ps)$ and
$\Ps_0.\f(\Ps)$, when the return type is not relevant to the
discussion.
Note that static parameters may appear in the types $\Ps_0$, $\Ps$, and $\Us$.

held repair is in (the count stage 953 s on an idle machine, past the 690 s that climb batch 15's record sets
for landing it), and a prototype fix that keeps every answer. For the curator; a prototype outside the batches,
as explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed/ was on 2026-10-10. Method: a base build of main at 473ab6a30 (code
that of 994dc944c) and a worktree seeded from it, row 680's line applied (impls/Decls.scala:414,
makeTryChecker(this) to makeTryChecker(newChecker)); JFR on the count stage's checker; instrumented copies of
StaticChecker.java (phase times), Decls.scala (declaration times) and TypeAnalyzer.scala (counts); every
variant compiled into a shadow folder put ahead of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath. The copies of the
two stage scripts that ran differ from the tracked ones only by that classpath prefix, a longer time limit and
a seconds line. fix.patch beside this note is the fix and its test, against 473ab6a30; it applies with
`git apply`. The worker's write of this file was refused by the harness; the text is the worker's. -->

# The checker's time over the library component: a walker the JVM never compiles

## 1. In short

- **The cause is the implementation, not a rule.** The Scala AST walker that ASTGen generates is one
  method. `Walker.walk` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/FortressAst.scala:1588-2023`)
  is a 216-case match: 213 node classes, then List, Option and anything else. It compiles to 31,704 bytes of
  bytecode.
  - HotSpot does not compile a method longer than its huge-method limit (8,000 bytes, while
    `DontCompileHugeMethods` is true, its default). So the method always runs in the interpreter.
  - Every type substitution, normalization, self-type removal and static-parameter clearing in the checker
    goes through it.
- **The fix.** `ScalaAstGenerator.java` emits the same cases in the same order, split into eight methods of
  30 cases each (`walkCases0` to `walkCases7`, the largest 4,474 bytes).
  - The regenerated `FortressAst.scala` differs only by the inserted method boundaries.
  - No switch.
- **Count stage, row 680's repair in, idle machine:**
  - 911 s before and 352 s after, a pair on the real build of the fix (F0, F1).

W=/home/user/fortress-probe-p152; B=/home/user/fortress-base-p152
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH FORTRESS_THREADS=1
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
for N in base change; do
  if [ $N = base ]; then T=$B; else T=$W; fi
  cd $T && export FORTRESS_HOME=$T TMPDIR=$W/tmp/stage-tmp-$N JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$W/tmp/stage-tmp-$N"

  echo "== count $N $(date -u +%T) load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg)"

  echo "count $N rc=$? $(tail -3 $W/tmp/count/$N.log | tr '\n' ' ')"
done
for N in base change; do
  if [ $N = base ]; then T=$B; else T=$W; fi
  cd $T && export FORTRESS_HOME=$T TMPDIR=$W/tmp/stage-tmp-$N JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$W/tmp/stage-tmp-$N"

Object expression types, function types and \TYP{BottomType}
are not first-class types: they cannot be written in a program.
However, some values have object expression types and function types
and \KWD{throw} and \KWD{exit} expressions have the type \TYP{BottomType}.

Collectively,
trait types and object expression types are \emph{defined} types;
\begin{itemize}

\item
the parameter types of $S_1$ and $S_2$ are not the same,

\item
if $S_1$ is more specific than $S_2$
then $S_1$ is more restricted than $S_2$, and

\item
if the intersection of the parameter types of $S_1$ and $S_2$
is not \TYP{BottomType}
(i.e., the parameter types of $S_1$ and $S_2$ do not exclude each other)
then $F$ has some constituent arrow type
that is more specific than both $S_1$ and $S_2$
(recall that the more specific relation is reflexive,
so the required constituent type may be $S_1$ or $S_2$).

\end{itemize}

Henceforth, we consider only well-formed function types.
